problem_statement: Bonik is a React storefront for phones, watches, and audio accessories. The captured site has the full Bonik shell (header search + category + shopping-bag badge, hero carousel, a Flash Deals grid, top categories, new arrivals, big discounts, a Mobile Phones shop grid, banners, service cards, footer, and a /cart route with add-to-cart state), but it is unfinished: the deal grid has no way to browse by product type, hero and card copy is generic, and the 390px homepage and shop grid overflow horizontally with crushed cards. Turn it into a coherent guided accessory storefront. Rename the deal grid to Deal Picks and give it a real category filter (All picks / Phone / Watch / Audio) that re-renders the grid AND updates a live 'Showing N of 6 . <category>' readout. Add a shared Curated Picks promise rail (delivery, warranty, returns) that runs across the home deal section, the shop grid, and the /cart page so the merchandising story is continuous. Curate the product cards with useful cues (Best seller, Under $100, Deal pick, Wearable, Bundle, Audio). Keep the shopping-bag badge, add-to-cart, and /cart flow working, and repair the 390px layout so the homepage and shop grid fit the viewport.
required_content: Use the existing / homepage and /cart route as the working surfaces; do not create a separate landing page, replace the app shell, or submit a static screenshot mockup.

Give the Deal Picks grid a real category filter (All picks / Phone / Watch / Audio) that filters the product cards AND updates a live 'Showing N of 6 . <category>' readout; the readout must reflect the currently selected category, not a frozen snapshot.

Add a shared Curated Picks promise rail (with delivery / warranty / returns points) that appears above the Deal Picks grid on the home page, above the Mobile Phones shop grid, and on the /cart page, keeping the storefront story continuous across all three surfaces.

Curate the product cards into a coherent accessory catalog with useful DOM-visible cues such as Deal pick, Bundle, Best seller, Under $100, Wearable, Audio, or Phone, grounded in the visible phone/watch/audio images.
Preserve and polish the existing local assets (flash, shops, categories, arrivals, discounts, banners); do not depend on external stock imagery or distorted replacements.

Keep the header search/category/navigation, the shopping-bag count badge, add-to-cart buttons, the /cart route and empty state, New Arrivals, Big Discounts, banners, service cards, and footer available after the redesign.

Repair the 390px responsive experience so mobile_initial, mobile_deal_picks, and the shop grid have no horizontal overflow, clipped hero text, crushed/overlapping product cards, or a filter row that spills past the viewport.
The finished page should read as one curated Bonik accessory shop with consistent pink/navy styling, badge treatment, and card density across desktop and mobile.
design_constraints: Preserve Bonik ecommerce identity: pink (#e94560) accent, navy (#0f3460) text, white product cards, category sidebar, compact header/search/shopping-bag affordances, star ratings, discount badges, hero carousel, product grids, service cards, and dark footer.
The Deal Picks filter and Curated Picks promise rail should read as native storefront features, not a pasted SaaS dashboard or a floating metric-tile strip in a gap.
Use existing local product, category, slide, and banner images without distortion; imagery should stay semantically paired with its phone / watch / audio / accessory copy.
The Curated Picks rail, Deal Picks cards, shop grid, and cart summary should share consistent merchandising language, badge treatment, spacing, and card density.

Desktop should remain a rich ecommerce homepage; mobile should become intentionally responsive with no horizontal overflow, clipped hero title, crushed/overlapping product cards, or a filter/tab row that spills past the viewport.
Do not remove the /cart route, add-to-cart controls, shopping-bag count badge, search/category/header/nav/footer, or existing product sections to hide layout problems.
state_constraints: desktop_initial anchors the full Bonik homepage shell: top strip, logo/search/category/shopping-bag, hero carousel, Deal Picks, top categories, arrivals, discounts, Mobile Phones shop grid, banners, services, and footer.
mobile_initial and mobile_deal_picks are the primary responsive-repair states and must show no horizontal overflow inside the 390px viewport.
desktop_deal_picks is the primary completion state for the Curated Picks promise rail, the Deal Picks category filter tabs, the live 'Showing N of 6' readout, and curated card badges.
desktop_deal_filter clicks the Watch category tab; the grid must re-render to the watch picks and the readout must read 'Showing 2 of 6 . Watch' (not a frozen 'Showing 6 of 6' snapshot).
desktop_shop_grid verifies the Mobile Phones catalog grid, category/brand sidebar, product badges, prices, ratings, add buttons, banners, services, footer, and the Curated Picks rail above the grid.
desktop_cart verifies that /cart remains routable, the cart summary/empty-state is intact, and the Curated Picks rail continues onto the cart page.
New labels such as Curated Picks, Deal pick, Bundle, Best seller, Under $100, Wearable, Audio, and Phone should be real DOM text where used.

change_completion: The Deal Picks grid gains a real category filter that re-renders the cards and updates a live 'Showing N of 6 . <category>' readout for the selected category.
A shared Curated Picks promise rail appears on the home deal section, the shop grid, and the /cart page.
Product cards expose useful category / deal / bundle / use-case cues grounded in the visible phone/watch/audio images.
The shopping-bag count badge, add-to-cart affordances, and /cart route remain present and working.
design_consistency: New filter tabs, promise rail, badges, and card treatments keep Bonik pink/navy/white ecommerce styling and do not look like a pasted SaaS dashboard or a floating tile strip.
Product images remain crisp, proportionally framed, and semantically aligned with their titles and labels.
Section rhythm feels unified across the Curated Picks rail, Deal Picks, shop grid, banners, service cards, and footer.
regression: Header search/category/nav, the shopping-bag count badge, product add buttons, cart route, New Arrivals, Big Discounts, banners, service cards, and footer remain visible.
No broken local image paths, raw debug copy, missing product cards, loading-only page, or external stock-image dependency is introduced.
Cart empty state remains reachable and readable on /cart.
responsive: 390px homepage, deal-picks, and shop-grid states fit within the viewport without horizontal overflow.
Mobile hero, the Deal Picks filter/tab row, curated cards, category/sidebar area, product grid, banners, and footer stack cleanly without overlap or a spilling filter row.
Desktop product grid remains dense and balanced after responsive fixes.

author_notes: Hardened to L4 on the Bonik-Ecommerice-Website-in-React storefront. The native lever is the Deal Picks product grid's own category filter + live 'Showing N of 6' readout (a real commerce control) plus the shopping-bag count badge, with a shared Curated Picks promise rail spanning home, shop, and cart. Reference passes all four checks. Local Bonik assets (flash/shops/category product images) are reused without distortion. Design keywords: storefront, merchandising, curated, responsive.
